title: Best Free LLM API for RAG in 2026 (No Credit Card)
description: Build retrieval-augmented generation on a free LLM API. Which providers suit RAG, free embedding models, rate-limit trade-offs, plus a Python starter.
author: freellm.site
content:
For retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on a budget, the best free LLM API has a **large context window and steady rate limits**. Google Gemini, with a 1M-token window and free embeddings, is the most complete free option, and Groq is the fastest for short-context answers. RAG feeds your own documents into the model at query time, so the generation model matters as much as the retrieval step.

RAG needs two pieces: an embedding model to index your documents and a chat model to answer. You can get both for free, although most free LLM APIs in our directory focus on **generation**. For embeddings, Google's `gemini-embedding-2` is free on the Gemini API free tier.

## What makes a free LLM API good for RAG?

A good RAG generation model has enough context for your retrieved passages plus the question, and rate limits that can handle real query traffic. Context size is rarely a problem now (Gemini Flash offers 1M tokens and Groq's free models 131K), so the choice usually comes down to [rate limits](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/).

RAG keeps prompts smaller than you might expect, because you retrieve only the few passages relevant to each question instead of stuffing in whole documents. That matters on Groq's free plan, which caps you at **8,000 tokens per minute** (plus 30 requests per minute and 1,000 per day): a request carrying 5K tokens of retrieved context leaves room for about one query a minute. On Groq, keep retrieval to a few short chunks, and send long-context queries to Gemini. If your retrieved chunks run long, see which providers offer the [largest context windows](/blog/free-llm-api-largest-context-window/).

## How does RAG work on a free LLM API?

RAG has three steps: index your documents, retrieve the pieces relevant to a question, then ask the model with those pieces as context.

The flow looks like this:

- **Index once.** Split documents into chunks and store them, usually as embeddings in a vector store.
- **Retrieve per query.** Embed the user's question and find the chunks closest to it.
- **Generate.** Send the question plus the retrieved chunks to a free LLM API and return the answer.

The generation call is a normal chat completion, so any [OpenAI-compatible provider](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) works with the same code.

## Free embeddings for indexing

The Gemini API's current embedding model is `gemini-embedding-2`, which Google lists as free on the free tier. It returns 3,072-dimension vectors by default. Older IDs are being retired: `text-embedding-004` shut down on 2026-01-14, the `gemini-embedding-2-preview` preview on 2026-08-10, and `gemini-embedding-001` is scheduled to shut down on 2028-05-14. The embedding spaces of `gemini-embedding-001` and `gemini-embedding-2` are incompatible, so re-embed everything if you switch.

```python
# pip install google-genai numpy
import numpy as np
from google import genai

gemini = genai.Client(api_key="YOUR_GEMINI_KEY")

def embed(texts):
    result = gemini.models.embed_content(model="gemini-embedding-2", contents=texts)
    return np.array([e.values for e in result.embeddings])

chunks = ["Refunds are accepted within 30 days.", "Shipping takes 3-5 business days."]
chunk_vectors = embed(chunks)  # index once, store alongside the chunks

def retrieve(question, k=3):
    q = embed([question])[0]
    scores = chunk_vectors @ q / (np.linalg.norm(chunk_vectors, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(q))
    return [chunks[i] for i in np.argsort(scores)[::-1][:k]]
```

For small collections an in-memory array like this is enough; move to a vector database once you have more than a few thousand chunks. If you prefer Cohere, its trial key (no card, 1,000 API calls a month) serves `embed-v4.0` through the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint as its chat models.

## A minimal RAG generation call

Here's the generation step against a free provider, using the `retrieve()` function above:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1", api_key="YOUR_GROQ_KEY")

def answer(question):
    context = "\n\n".join(retrieve(question))  # keep this short: Groq's free plan is 8K tokens/minute
    prompt = f"Use only this context to answer.\n\nContext:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}"
    return client.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
        reasoning_effort="low",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    ).choices[0].message.content

print(answer("What is the refund window?"))
```

To run generation on Gemini instead, change the base URL to `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`, use your Gemini key, set the model to `gemini-3.8-flash`, and remove the `reasoning_effort` line.

## Which free provider should you use for RAG?

Use [Groq](/providers/groq/) when answer speed matters and the retrieved context is small: retrieval is fast and Groq's generation is near-instant, so the app feels quick. Use [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) when the retrieved context is large, since its 1M-token window takes long passages without running into a per-minute token cap as low as Groq's. [Cohere](/providers/cohere/) is also worth a look, because its models are built for retrieval and grounded answers. Our [Groq vs Google Gemini comparison](/compare/groq-vs-google_gemini/) covers the trade-offs in detail.

All three need no card, so you can prototype a full RAG pipeline for free. Browse the [directory](/) to compare them, and put a second provider behind the first as a rate-limit fallback for production traffic.

faq.q: Can you build RAG with a free LLM API?
faq.a: Yes. RAG's generation step is a standard chat completion, so any free OpenAI-compatible provider like Groq or Google Gemini works, and Gemini's gemini-embedding-2 model is free on the Gemini API free tier. With an in-memory index or a free vector store, a full RAG prototype can cost nothing to run.

faq.q: Do free LLM APIs include embeddings for RAG?
faq.a: Some do. Google's Gemini API offers gemini-embedding-2 free of charge on its free tier, and Cohere's no-card trial key serves embed-v4.0 within its 1,000 calls a month. Many other free tiers, including Groq's, focus on chat generation, so you pair them with a separate embedding model.

faq.q: How big a context window does RAG need?
faq.a: Usually less than you would think. Retrieval sends only the few relevant chunks into the prompt, so a 128K window is plenty for most RAG apps. The tighter limit on free tiers is often tokens per minute: Groq's free plan allows 8K, so keep retrieved context short there or use Gemini's 1M-token window.
